stages.reference:
Create a close visual reference for spruce foliage in a cold grounded dark-fantasy forest. The foliage consists of dense needle-bearing sprays built around tough narrow twigs. Needles should feel short, stiff and numerous, forming layered shadowy masses with subtle differences between older deep green growth and slightly lighter exposed tips. Cold, wind and age leave restrained dry needles and weathered twig surfaces within the living canopy. Favor deep muted blue-green, forest green and cool gray-green. Avoid fluffy pine-needle brushes, Christmas-tree brightness, snow decoration, giant individual needles or uniform synthetic branching. Establish the compact, cold-resistant material language of spruce foliage—dark, sharp, layered and resilient—without copying branch composition into the eventual texture.

FOLIAGE POROSITY: Preserve approximately the original texture's overall opaque-to-transparent area ratio, not its alpha mask. Freely redesign every gap's position, shape and distribution, as well as leaf clusters and overlaps. Keep genuine fully transparent openings between foliage; do not fill the whole square with continuous leaf material or render a solid cube face. No exact pixel or silhouette tracing. Retain neutral, runtime-tint-friendly value detail where applicable.
